name: Haiku concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Pure AI infrastructure supply-chain focus emphasizing semiconductor equipment and design leadership (ASML, AVGO, AMD) with tactical cloud/platform exposure (SNOW), positioned for Q4 2026 datacenter capex acceleration while maintaining 16% cash for volatility management.
reassessment_note: Shifting from platform-software-heavy positioning (R2: MSFT 18%, SNOW 16%, CRM 10%) to pure supply-chain infrastructure leadership. Market data shows semiconductor equipment (ASML, AVGO) and chip designers (AMD) are primary beneficiaries of sustained AI capex cycle, with ASML up 1.91% and analyst support strong. Reducing software overlap with Round 2 from ~57% to ~34% to satisfy novelty requirement while maintaining AI infrastructure thesis. Treasury yield volatility (10-yr at 5.21%) and industry calls for development restraint justify elevated cash (16%) and continued risk management through stops/take-profits. SNOW's 35% revenue growth and guidance raise (reported Sept 2) demonstrate platform thesis still valid but now overweighted in R2, allowing R3 to focus on supply-chain multiplier effect.

positions.thesis: Pure capex leverage play. ASML's EUV lithography equipment is indispensable for all next-generation AI chip manufacturing (both NVIDIA and AMD rely on these tools). As hyperscalers accelerate capex in Q4 2026, ASML receives direct demand boost before chip designers themselves. Positioned at $1,743.94, trading with strong 2026 momentum and consensus analyst rating supports higher allocation.

Broadcom supplies critical semiconductor interconnect, infrastructure, and networking for data centers. At $355.14 with consensus Buy rating and $527 PT, positioned to benefit directly from AI capex cycle for both processor interconnects and data center networking. Adds diversification to semiconductor exposure alongside AMD.

AI processor design leadership competing directly in data center CPUs and AI accelerators against NVIDIA. At $630.63 with 2.45% leg gain since entry, AMD benefits from both AI capex cycle and competitive dynamics creating multiple paths to outperformance. October 14 earnings will be key catalyst.

Mobile and edge AI processor exposure. QCOM at $201.97 provides exposure to smartphone AI features and edge computing infrastructure, diversifying away from pure data center concentration. Beneficial if AI deployment accelerates beyond cloud to mobile devices.

Platform-layer AI infrastructure. Snowflake at $335.94 reported 35% revenue growth and raised full-year guidance to 36% (Sept 2 earnings). Essential database for AI workloads but reduced from 16% to 12% to lower platform overlap with Round 2. Maintains exposure to high-growth AI-enabling software without concentration risk.

Enterprise AI adoption play through CRM suite. At $234.02 with 27.4% leg gain, CRM validates enterprise AI platform thesis but reduced to 6% from 10% to create clear differentiation from Round 2 (which carries 9.96%). Maintains optionality on enterprise software AI wave without redundancy.

AI platform and infrastructure operator via Azure cloud and Copilot integration. MSFT at $516.17 rallied 3.7% on Sept 25 after new Copilot features, demonstrating platform momentum. Significantly reduced from 18% to 6% to avoid platform concentration with Round 2. Maintains access to enterprise AI transition without redundancy.

AI semiconductor flagship but core holding, not concentration play. At $225.07 with 12.24% leg gain, NVDA is included for completion of AI infrastructure exposure but maintained at modest 7% weight. Current valuation and concentration concerns justify reduced weighting vs. R2 (8%) given supply-chain diversification now provided by ASML/AVGO/AMD.
